# Implementation Readiness Checklist: Grammar Vertical Slice

**Purpose**: Assess whether the Grammar Vertical Slice requirements are complete, unambiguous, architecture-aligned, and ready for task generation and PR review.
**Created**: 2026-10-10
**Feature**: [Grammar Vertical Slice specification](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirements Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements and acceptance scenarios defined for every transition in the primary flow from Home through topic and lesson selection, exercise submission, feedback, and the next sentence? [Completeness, Spec §User Stories 1–5, Spec §FR-001–FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Are alternate and recovery requirements complete for correct feedback, incorrect feedback, Fix, Next, feedback minimization/reopening, grading cancellation, and the final sentence? [Scenario Coverage, Spec §FR-013–FR-017, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK003 Are duplicate submission, cancellation, and late grading-result semantics stated precisely enough to determine which response and progress state remain authoritative? [Clarity, Edge Case, Spec §FR-008–FR-009, Plan §Grammar state machine]
- [ ] CHK004 Are data-availability requirements complete for populated catalogs, empty topic and lesson collections, unavailable identifiers, and the minimum authored topic/lesson/exercise set? [Coverage, Spec §FR-021, Spec §Assumptions, Contract §Catalog and lookup behavior]
- [ ] CHK005 Are grading normalization rules exhaustive and unambiguous for case, leading/trailing whitespace, repeated internal whitespace, punctuation, word order, Unicode text, and accepted alternatives? [Clarity, Edge Case, Spec §FR-010–FR-012]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the boundary between localized EN/VI product chrome and unchanged authored English lesson content defined for every picker, list, exercise, loading, feedback, empty, and unavailable state? [Completeness, Consistency, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the final-sentence outcome and all excluded completion, reward, persistence, authentication, payment, AI, and backend behaviors mutually consistent across scope, functional requirements, and success criteria? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope, Spec §FR-022–FR-023]
- [ ] CHK008 Does the specification state whether local catalog or grading operations can fail unexpectedly and, if so, define the error and recovery requirements; otherwise, is their infallibility documented as an assumption? [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-010, Plan §Mock repository boundary]
- [ ] CHK009 Can every functional requirement be traced to at least one independently reviewable acceptance scenario or measurable success criterion, including cancellation, empty states, localization, and final-sentence behavior? [Traceability, Measurability, Spec §FR-001–FR-023, Spec §SC-001–SC-007]

## Design-System Reuse

- [ ] CHK010 Is every Grammar surface and state mapped to the required canonical components—TopicCard, LessonCard/Grammar, ProgressStepper/Grammar, SourceTextCard/Sentence, AnswerInput, SubmitButton, HintChipBar, ExerciseTemplate, and all three FeedbackSheet variants? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Plan §Reusable design-system surface]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the required states and responsibilities of each reused component specified clearly enough to distinguish component behavior from Grammar screen composition? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006–FR-017, Plan §Design Decisions]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the prohibition on canonical component duplication explicit for visual copies, feature-local wrappers that reproduce component behavior, and Grammar-specific forks of shared components? [Clarity, Architecture Boundary, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK013 Are all proposed design-system extensions identified as narrow, additive, backward-compatible changes with clear ownership and no Grammar domain semantics leaking into shared APIs? [Completeness, Consistency, Plan §Reusable design-system surface]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the GrammarCorrect requirement for a visible but disabled AI-analysis action reconciled explicitly with the canonical FeedbackSheet contract and its current variants? [Conflict, Spec §FR-013, Plan §Reusable design-system surface]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the requirement to update canonical design-system documentation or tokens before dependent Flutter APIs stated for every identified contract gap? [Dependency, Plan §Constitution Check, Plan §Reusable design-system surface]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the minimum loading duration tied to a named canonical motion token, with a documented requirements path if no 300 ms token currently exists? [Clarity, Dependency, Spec §FR-009, Plan §Reusable design-system surface]
- [ ] CHK017 Are canonical background/foreground palette pairing, typography, spacing, radii, breakpoints, motion, focus, and state-token requirements defined without allowing feature-local arbitrary values? [Coverage, Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Constitution §Design System]
- [ ] CHK018 Are conditional shared additions such as PagerDots/Lesson, reusable empty-state treatment, instruction slots, focus handles, and adaptive sheet constraints resolved as mandatory, excluded, or contingent on a clearly stated requirement? [Ambiguity, Plan §Reusable design-system surface]

## Architecture Boundaries

- [ ] CHK019 Are ownership and dependency requirements explicit for Grammar, Writing, app routing, design_system, core, localization, and generated API code, including the prohibition on Grammar importing Writing internals? [Completeness, Plan §Constitution Check, Constitution §Dependency Direction]
- [ ] CHK020 Are Grammar domain requirements constrained to pure Dart concepts without Flutter, Riverpod, routing, localization, JSON, storage, platform, or generated-client dependencies? [Architecture Boundary, Plan §Grammar-specific code, Constitution §Dependency Direction]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the Grammar repository contract defined as the source-of-truth boundary for catalog retrieval, lesson retrieval, exercise lookup, and deterministic grading, with presentation isolated from data implementation details? [Completeness, Plan §Mock repository boundary, Contract §GrammarRepository]
- [ ] CHK022 Is deterministic in-memory grading explicitly limited to this client-only slice while production grading remains backend-owned, with no conflicting implication that client grading becomes production authority? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, Plan §Production grading seam, Constitution §Backend Authority]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the sealed workflow state model complete for editing, grading, correct feedback, incorrect feedback, cancellation, retry/fix, reopening, progression, and terminal return, without mutually exclusive boolean states? [Completeness, Consistency, Plan §Grammar state machine]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements for stale request identity, duplicate interaction handling, cancellation, and exactly-once progression precise enough to preserve deterministic state transitions? [Clarity, Edge Case, Spec §FR-009, Spec §FR-016, Plan §Grammar state machine]
- [ ] CHK025 Are typed-route ownership, route parameters, invalid topic/lesson/exercise handling, stable semantic routes, and final return behavior documented consistently across specification and plan? [Completeness, Consistency, Spec §FR-001–FR-004, Spec §FR-023, Plan §Routing]
- [ ] CHK026 Are exclusions against new dependencies, premature application/use-case layers, generic shared Exercise domain abstractions, Base* abstractions, persistence, and sensitive answer logging explicit and mutually consistent? [Boundary, Spec §FR-022, Plan §Design Decisions, Constitution §Code Quality]

## Adaptive and Accessibility Requirements

- [ ] CHK027 Is the mapping from compact/medium/expanded product terminology to canonical window-size classes and breakpoints explicit, without device-identity assumptions? [Clarity, Consistency, Spec §FR-019, Plan §Adaptive behavior]
- [ ] CHK028 Are layout requirements separately defined for the topic picker, lesson list, exercise, and feedback surfaces across all required size classes, including reflow, content width, action placement, and scroll behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, Plan §Adaptive behavior]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for constrained height, resizable macOS windows, on-screen keyboards, long Vietnamese strings, and large text without obscuring content or actions? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §FR-019–FR-020, Plan §Adaptive behavior]
- [ ] CHK030 Are interaction requirements complete for touch, mouse, trackpad, hover, keyboard focus, Enter/Space activation, Escape dismissal, and logical Tab traversal on every interactive surface? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, Constitution §Adaptive UI]
- [ ] CHK031 Are semantic names, roles, progress announcements, grading status, verdict announcements, and error/help text requirements specified for assistive technologies? [Completeness, Accessibility, Spec §FR-020, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK032 Are focus-placement and focus-restoration requirements unambiguous after opening or dismissing feedback, choosing Fix, choosing Next, canceling grading, and returning to the lesson list? [Clarity, Recovery Flow, Spec §FR-009, Spec §FR-015–FR-017]
- [ ] CHK033 Is the disabled AI-analysis action's reason, discoverability, semantic disabled state, focus policy, and localized explanation fully specified without implying that AI analysis is available? [Completeness, Accessibility, Spec §FR-013, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK034 Are non-color verdict cues, contrast, target size, reading order, and visible focus requirements tied to objective canonical accessibility criteria for all size classes? [Measurability, Spec §FR-020, Spec §SC-005–SC-006]

## Writing Regression Requirements

- [ ] CHK035 Is “Writing remains unchanged” defined across observable copy, visual appearance, component variants, state transitions, grading, navigation, accessibility semantics, and adaptive behavior? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-001, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK036 Are the permitted Home-surface additions constrained so the Grammar entry can be introduced without changing the existing Writing entry's content, order, callback contract, or route semantics? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Plan §Writing regression verification]
- [ ] CHK037 Do requirements for shared design-system API extensions specify backward-compatible defaults that preserve all existing Writing call sites and visual states? [Consistency, Dependency, Plan §Reusable design-system surface, Plan §Writing regression verification]
- [ ] CHK038 Are acceptable and unacceptable changes to existing Writing golden baselines defined, including how an intentional shared design-system correction would be distinguished from a regression? [Ambiguity, Measurability, Plan §Writing regression verification]
- [ ] CHK039 Is the required regression evidence identified for Writing provider/ViewModel behavior, widgets, routes, goldens, localization, and architecture boundaries without relying only on the new Grammar flow? [Completeness, Traceability, Plan §Tests, Plan §Writing regression verification]
- [ ] CHK040 Is the zero-observable-change criterion reconciled with unavoidable shared generated localization or design-system artifacts, including which file changes are permitted and which require explicit review? [Consistency, Boundary, Spec §SC-007, Plan §Writing regression verification]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when the requirement is missing, ambiguous, conflicting, or not objectively reviewable; add the resolution beside the item or link to the relevant artifact change.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist state but does not modify these markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate lifecycle managed by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Items are globally numbered for stable review comments and traceability.
